message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I don’t see a clear STEMI pattern on this ECG**, though a single image cannot rule out an acute heart attack.

My reading:
- Regular sinus rhythm, approximately **50 beats/minute**.
- Narrow QRS complexes with prominent chest-lead voltage.
- Upright T waves, but **no convincing diagnostic ST elevation in adjacent leads or clear reciprocal ST depression**. The rise toward the T waves in V2–V4 should not be mistaken for ST elevation.

STEMI criteria assess elevation at the **J point—the end of the QRS**, rather than the T-wave height. [ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If there is current or recent chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, or fainting, seek emergency assessment now**; repeat ECGs and troponin testing may be needed even with this tracing.

What prompted the ECG, and what are the patient’s age and symptoms?
